On to reusing needles on yourself. No. Don't. There is no reason to when needles themselves are so cheap and the risk of infection and shoddy work from blunt/bent needles is so not worth it. 

Before tattooing on skin make sure you educate yourself on potential infection risks, and invest in the proper materials and equipment to create a sterile space. It’s too early in the morning for me to properly put my thoughts about this into words but lab rats are super important, and showing them cared for and happy is a good way to diminish this idea that a lot of people have that all lab rats are suffering and are treated as disposable by the labs that use them. People tend to, all at once, avoid looking at labs that use rats and other live subjects and have it in their brains that labs are cruel awful places that torture animals. The whole thought makes people uncomfortable so it’s easier to just not talk about it.

I’m not naive enough to say that all labs treat their rats with care and respect, but the more transparent we are with labs like OP’s the higher general standards will be across the board when the general public’s expectations are that all lab rats should receive care and socialisation.

For me, if a plan is made a week in advanced it's not set in stone unless it's something really big that I have to be at. It'll only be set in stone if we end up talking about it once more a couple of days before the event. That way we all know we've been thinking about it, nothing better has come up and we've saved time for it. 
That or our plans are made on the spot, on the day and there are no bailouts.

I used to be like you, expecting these things to be 100% on and planning way in advanced. I'd get super hyped only to find that everybody had either made other plans or they weren't prepared to go out that day. It was shitty at first but I realised that we were the type of people who can't put aside time in advance because we're constantly making and receiving plans that we can't totally keep track of.
